title.narrative: Support to Upper Secondary Reform in Brazil Operation

description.narrative: The Program Development Objectives (PDO) are to (i) strengthen the capacity of the state secretariats of education to implement theupper secondary reform, prioritizing vulnerable schools, (ii) support the expansion of the Full-Time School Program in Brazil's territory, and (iii) support the response to the COVID-19 pandemic in the Upper Secondary Education schools.

The development objective of the Support to the Upper Secondary Education Reform Operation Project for Brazil is to strengthen the capacity of the state secretariats of education to implement the upper secondary reform, prioritizing vulnerable schools, and to increase the index of basic education development in targeted fulltime upper secondary schools in Brazil's territory. This operation is consistent with the emerging priorities of the new Brazil country partnership framework (CPF) for the Federative Republic of Brazil in which the education sector is explicitly mentioned as a key area of intervention within the first focus area - fiscal consolidation and government effectiveness. The program complies with the criteria for prioritizing the World Bank engagement by combining government demand with the World Bank's comparative advantage. The design and implementation of the upper secondary education reform require a focus on institutions and capacity building, as well as incentives for achieving results. The program has three key indicators: (a) number of states where at least 40 percent of schools have implemented the new curricula; (b) number of states where at least 50 percent of vulnerable schools have implemented the new curricula; and (c) percentage change in the basic education development index (IDEB) in targeted full-time school (FTS).

title.narrative: PDO 4: Number of enrolled students in upper-secondary schools participating in the FTS program. (Number)

comment.narrative: The end target was achieved in 2022, but the enrollment in the national upper secondary FTS program decreased in 2023. The extension of the loan agreement, from December 2023 to December 2024, allowed the Project perceives the reduction in the coverage of FTS Program because the withdrawal of schools from the Program and the drop in enrollment. The states reported that the drop in enrollment was caused by the need of students to work due to the worsening economic situation of families. Thus, although in the years 2021 and 2022 the FTS Program reached more than 350 thousand enrollments, in 2023 this achievement was not observed, leaving about 10 thousand enrollments below the established goal. In addition, the non-publication of new Ordinances of adhesion in the FTS Program since 2019 implied in the impossibility of expanding enrollment in the program through the introduction of new schools.

title.narrative: PDO 5: Implementation of a safe and effective reopening of upper-secondary schools (Text)

target.value: Offer of distance education as part of an hybrid model in, at least, 15 States.

comment.narrative: This indicator is composed of two components: (i) Key measures to support the safe reopening of NEM schools are implemented, which is already achieved; (ii) Distance education as part of a hybrid model is offered in at least 15 States. This PDO has been achieved, considering that the national Portaria on Hybrid Education was issued and signed on November 8, 2022. The implementation of hybrid education (Rede de Inovação para Aprendizagem Hibrida) has been achieved with the signing of Commitment Agreements for the participation in the program and the offering of hybrid education in 16 states.

actual.value: Key measures to support safe reopening of NEM schools are implemented.

title.narrative: PDO 4: Number of enrolled students in upper-secondary schools participating in the FTS program. (Number)

comment.narrative: The end target was achieved in 2022, but the enrollment in the national upper secondary FTS program decreased in 2023. MEC assumes that the implementation of new FTS program of MEC that support the expansion of FTS for also primary and lower secondary education interfered in the expansion of FTS coverage in upper secondary. The rate of achievement for this indicator is 96 percent - calculated as the ratio between the increase from baseline to date (246,046) to the expected target increase through project closure (256,273).

baseline.value: Rigorous analysis not conducted and best practice disseminated

title.narrative: IRI 1.19 (DLI 16): Strengthening schools connectivity through the provision of necessary equipment for hybrid education to promote learning recovery strategies.

target.value: (i) 20 states with media centers installed with equipment needed to deliver hybrid education (ii) 1,000 vulnerable schools with school kits needed to deliver hybrid education

comment.narrative: This indicator was partially achieved. Target (i) was partially achieved and target (ii) was not achieved. Target (i) (20 states with media centers installed with equipment needed to deliver hybrid education) will be partially achieved because of delays in the installation of media centers by the states. 16 media centers were installed. Target (ii) (1,000 vulnerable schools with school kits needed to deliver hybrid education) was not achieved because of the cancelation of the procurement process by FNDE.

title.narrative: IRI 1.19 (DLI 16): Strengthening schools connectivity through the provision of necessary equipment for hybrid education to promote learning recovery strategies.

target.value: (i) 20 states with media centers installed with equipment needed to deliver hybrid education (ii) 1,000 vulnerable schools with school kits needed to deliver hybrid education

comment.narrative: This indicator is expected to be partially achieved. Target (i) will be partially achieve and target (ii) will not be achieved. Target (i) (20 states with media centers installed with equipment needed to deliver hybrid education) will be partially achieved because of delays in the installation of media centers by the states. MECs expects that 15 media centers will be installed by December 30, 2024. Target (ii) (1,000 vulnerable schools with school kits needed to deliver hybrid education) will not be achieved because of the cancelation of the procurement process by FNDE.
